inventory.sourceFigureDescription: PURE-VECTOR FIGURE, no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM-read at 120dpi, staging-pubh4/vlm-census.txt — VLM available this session): the lead-in sentence 'Definitions and formulas are based on the classic 2 × 2 or contingency table.', then the bordered 2×2 grid — column header 'Disease or outcome' with ⊕ over the disease column and ⊖ over the no-disease column; row label 'Exposure or intervention' printing VERTICALLY down the left side with ⊕ beside the exposed row and ⊖ beside the unexposed row; cells a (top-left, exposed + diseased), b (top-right), c (bottom-left), d (bottom-right). Above/around it, three stacked formula labels: 'Odds ratio = a/c ÷ b/d = ad/bc', 'Relative risk = a/(a + b) ÷ c/(c + d)', 'Attributable risk = a/(a + b) − c/(c + d)' — present in the text layer but visually obscured in the digital render (the teal running-header band is drawn over the top two; the third prints white-on-white; pdftoppm + pdftocairo agree) with the banner fragment 'AND BIOSTATISTICS' interleaving the c/(c + d) fraction in the text layer.

inventory.visualPurpose: The Quantifying risk table (book 258): the eight-measure reference — columns TERm / DEFINITION / EXAmPLE / FORmULA, from Odds ratio (case-control, ad/bc, the red 'You take a case to the OR.') through Case fatality rate (deaths/cases × 100), each row with definition, worked example, and formula — the arithmetic core of epidemiology and biostatistics
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: COLOR-CODED TABLE, no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM-read at 120dpi, staging-pubh4/vlm-census.txt — VLM available this session): the table title 'Quantifying risk', four column headers (TERm / DEFINITION / EXAmPLE / FORmULA — small-caps artifacts as printed), then EIGHT rows in printed order, each carried verbatim in the note's table block: (1) Odds ratio — case-control studies, odds of exposure among cases (a/c) vs controls (b/d), OR=1/>1/<1 interpretation lines, the 20/30-vs-5/25 smoking example → OR 8, the RED mnemonic 'You take a case to the OR.' (last line of the EXAMPLE cell), formula OR = a/c ÷ b/d = ad/bc with the worked grid a b = 20 5 / c d = 10 20 printed inside the FORMULA column; (2) Relative risk — cohort studies, risk in exposed ÷ unexposed, RR=1/>1/↓↑ lines, the 5/10-vs-1/10 radiation example → RR 5, 'For rare diseases (low prevalence), OR approximates RR.', formula RR = a/(a+b) ÷ c/(c+d) with the worked grid a b = 5 5 / c d = 1 9; (3) Relative risk reduction — proportion of risk reduction, ART vs ARC, flu-shot example RR = 2/8 = 0.25 and RRR = 0.75, formulas RRR = 1 – RR and (ARC – ART)/ARC; (4) Attributable risk — difference in risk between exposed and unexposed, smoking 21% vs 1% → 20%, formulas AR = a/(a+b) − c/(c+d) and AR% = (RR − 1)/RR × 100; (5) Absolute risk reduction — 'the difference in risk (not the proportion)', placebo 8% vs vaccine 2% → ARR = 8%–2% = 6% = 0.06, formula ARR = c/(c+d) − a/(a+b) (control minus treated, as printed); (6) Number needed to treat — 'Number of patients who need to be treated for 1 patient to benefit. Lower number = better treatment.', NNT = 1/ARR, NO example cell; (7) Number needed to harm — 'Number of patients who need to be exposed to a risk factor for 1 patient to be harmed. Higher number = safer exposure.', NNH = 1/AR with 'AR' in red, NO example cell; (8) Case fatality rate — 'Percentage of deaths occurring among those with disease.', 4 deaths among 10 meningitis cases = 40%, CFR% = deaths/cases × 100. TERM names print in bold dark blue; the header band is a shaded strip; no photos, margin notes, or asterisk footnotes.
inventory.kypLocation: Zone B of the registry visual (QuantifyingRiskMap in visuals/pubhealth-p4.tsx): the eight rows as measure cards in two columns (family chips RATIO / DIFFERENCE / RECIPROCAL / OUTCOME ONLY, each card carrying its printed formula, worked example, and interpretation strip, the OR and RR cards embedding the two printed worked grids), plus Zone C's RATIO · DIFFERENCE · RECIPROCAL grammar strip with the two attributed First Aid mnemonics; the full table's text is ALSO carried verbatim in the note's table block (blocks[1]), core.what, the decoder list block, and recall[0-8]
